# Jira mirror (SCRIBL)

Jira is the system of record for issue state. This file is the repo's mirror of
it. The write policy that requires the mirror is in `CLAUDE.md`, section
"Work-item execution (story/AC kit)"; mapping conventions are in
[Jira board](/jira-board).

Two rules govern it, and they are not equally strong:

1. Every Jira write gets a row in the write log below, whoever made it and
   whatever they used, and that row is committed in the same session as the
   write. Where the repo carries more about the issue than a log row, the
   story file under `tracking/stories/` and the card in `tracking/board.md`
   move in the same commit. A Jira write with no matching repo commit is an
   incomplete operation. Nothing checks this
   automatically today. A write that never got a row leaves no trace here, so
   the write log tells you what was declared, not what happened. Closing that
   gap means diffing the log against each issue's comment list and changelog;
   until someone builds it, treat the log as a record kept in good faith.
2. The issue table is regenerated from Jira, never hand-edited. Regenerate it
   and `git diff` to see drift. This one is checkable on demand, and it is
   the reason the table can be trusted where the log cannot.

## Regenerate and diff

With the `JIRA_*` environment variables from `scripts/jira-sync/README.md` set
(`JIRA_BASE_URL` is `https://bounteous.jira.com`):

```sh
curl -s -u "$JIRA_EMAIL:$JIRA_API_TOKEN" \
  --get "$JIRA_BASE_URL/rest/api/3/search/jql" \
  --data-urlencode 'jql=project = SCRIBL ORDER BY key ASC' \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=summary,status,assignee,labels,updated,issuetype' \
  --data-urlencode 'maxResults=100' \
  | jq -r '.issues[] | "| \(.key) | \(.fields.issuetype.name) | \(.fields.summary) | \(.fields.status.name) | \(.fields.assignee.displayName // "-") | \(if (.fields.labels|length)==0 then "-" else (.fields.labels|sort|join(" ")) end) | \(.fields.updated[0:10]) |"'
git diff -- tracking/jira-mirror.md
```

`/rest/api/3/search/jql` is the current Jira Cloud search endpoint; the old
`GET /rest/api/3/search` is gone.

It pages at 100 and the board is past 150, so one call silently returns a
partial table. Get the token and make the second call:

```sh
TOK=$(curl -s -u "$JIRA_EMAIL:$JIRA_API_TOKEN" \
  --get "$JIRA_BASE_URL/rest/api/3/search/jql" \
  --data-urlencode 'jql=project = SCRIBL ORDER BY key ASC' \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=summary' --data-urlencode 'maxResults=100' \
  | jq -r '.nextPageToken // empty')
```

then repeat the first command with `--data-urlencode "nextPageToken=$TOK"`
added, until the response carries no `nextPageToken`. Paste all the rows over
the table below in key order, then diff. If the row count does not match the
count in the heading, you paged wrong.

With the Atlassian MCP server or the Jira connector in the Claude desktop app
instead of credentials in a shell, run the same query through
`searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with the same JQL and field list, and the same jq
filter over the saved response.

Either way, check the connection before you promise anyone a Jira change.
`getAccessibleAtlassianResources` reports the sites you can reach and the
scopes you hold, so `write:jira-work` is something to confirm rather than
assume. With no connection at all, the repo side is still yours to change;
say that plainly instead of reporting a Jira write that never happened.

## Write log

One row per Jira write by an agent, in the order the writes happened. A
session that makes several writes appends several rows. Append, never rewrite:
a wrong row gets a later correcting row, not an edit, because an edited log is
a log nobody can date.

The Commit column holds the short SHA of the repo commit that pairs with the
write. It reads `self` when the write's only repo change is the row itself, in
which case the pairing commit is the one that added the row and `git log -1
--format=%h -- tracking/jira-mirror.md` finds it.

When a Jira write lands and the commit does not, the write is real and the
mirror is behind: commit the row on its own as soon as you notice, and say so
in the row. The reverse, a committed row for a write that failed, gets a
correcting row saying the write did not land.
